signin.title: Open your Drive
signin.lead: Your phone holds the key. Scan this code with the BIShare app and the key comes to this browser, sealed for it alone. No password, no email.
signin.step1Body: Go to Drive, then Drive account, then Open Drive on the web.
signin.step2Body: Point the phone at the code on the right, or type the letters under it.
signin.step3Body: The phone shows letters. If they match the ones here, tap Approve.
signin.stayBody: Stays open for 30 days of use. Leave it off on a computer you share: the Drive locks when you close the tab, and after 12 hours without use.
signin.qrLabel: Sign-in code for the BIShare app
signin.typeInstead: Or type these letters in the app
signin.waiting: Waiting for your phone · new code in {left}
signin.footer: Files are opened in this browser. BIShare's servers only ever see sealed bytes.

deletePage.title: Delete your BIShare Drive
deletePage.lead: Deleting the Drive removes everything in it for good: every file, folder and thumbnail, and every device's access. It is done in the BIShare app, so only someone who holds the Drive's key can do it.
deletePage.step1: Open BIShare on a phone or computer that has your Drive.
deletePage.step2: Go to Drive, then Drive account.
deletePage.step3: Tap Delete Drive account at the bottom.
deletePage.step4: Sign in with the same Apple or Google account to confirm. Deletion starts at once.
deletePage.whatBody: All files and folders, their thumbnails, the devices and browsers with access, and the link to your Apple or Google sign-in.
deletePage.keptBody: BIShare keeps no copy. Files were encrypted on your devices, so nobody, BIShare included, could have read them.
deletePage.subsBody: A paid plan is billed by the App Store or Google Play. Cancel it there too, in your store account's subscriptions.
deletePage.noDeviceBody: Install BIShare, sign in to Drive with the same Apple or Google account, then delete it there. If that does not work, write to support@billiongroup.net.

e2e.definition: Files are locked on your device with a key only your devices hold. BIShare stores them but can't open them.

key.definition: The secret that unlocks your files. It stays on your devices and is never sent to BIShare.

device.definition: A phone, computer or browser that holds your Drive key. Each one can open your files.

browser.definition: A web browser you signed in by scanning a code with the BIShare app. It keeps a copy of the key until it locks or is removed.

stay.definition: Keeps this browser open for 30 days of use. When off, it locks when you close the tab, or after 12 hours without use.

trash.definition: Deleted items wait here for 30 days so you can restore them. They still count toward your storage.

linked.definition: The same file was already in your Drive, so it was added without uploading it again and takes no extra space.

region.definition: Where your encrypted files are stored. It is chosen when the Drive is made.

thumbnail.definition: A small preview picture, made on your device and encrypted like the file itself.

plan.definition: How much space your Drive has. Plans are bought in the BIShare app; the web shows what you have.

phrase.definition: Words that bring back your Drive key if you lose all your devices. Only the BIShare app shows them.

quota.definition: The space your plan gives you. Files, folders and the trash all count; uploads in progress hold space until they finish.

kpiHelp.used: Everything stored in your Drive, including the trash and uploads in progress.
kpiHelp.files: Files in your Drive, not counting folders or the trash. The line below counts files added in the chosen period.
kpiHelp.media: Photos and videos in your Drive. They are also shown on the Photos page.
kpiHelp.trash: Space used by deleted items. Empty the trash to get it back now, or it frees itself after 30 days.
